title: Lesson 1: The OneAccord Digital Standard
completionTitle: You've completed Lesson 1: The OneAccord Digital Standard
keyConcepts: Why we standardize: less noise, searchable history, room to grow
Every tool has an intended use: five places work lives — email, channel posts, private chat, Ninety.io Headlines, the Hub
The quick test: does this need a record, a response, or a meeting?
A conversation in the wrong place can be moved without losing its history
The Standard exists so a decision survives a handover, a leave or a role change
nextTeaser: Next, Lesson 2 zooms in on Outlook: external contacts, formal records, and what to do with internal email chains.

blocks.html:
Three weeks into the role, a client asks why the project timeline changed in March. You were copied on the decision, so you go looking for it: 400 messages, eight with the same subject line, two versions of the plan attached, and the actual decision buried in a reply fourteen messages down.

You find it — twenty-five minutes later. And when you take two weeks' leave, whoever covers you will do the same hunt, with less context than you have.

None of that is anyone being careless. It's what happens when five tools are used without a shared answer to one question: where does this belong? This lesson gives you that answer in a sentence.

blocks.prompt: Before the map, your starting point. Where does the work you're doing this week actually live — your inbox, a chat, a channel, a document somewhere, or in someone's head? And where was the last decision you had to go hunting for? (Optional — skip if you'd rather go straight to the map.)

blocks.html:
By the end of this lesson you'll be able to:

  1. Decide, in a few seconds, where any piece of work belongs — using one question.
  2. Diagnose a conversation that's in the wrong place and move it without losing the history.
  3. Find the approved version of a policy or standard, rather than the version sitting in your inbox.

About 15 minutes, plus one short task in the tools themselves. This is the map for the six lessons that follow.

The same week, two ways

Both columns are a real week's work at OneAccord. Only one of them can be found again next month.

The week's workHandled out of the inboxHandled by the Standard
Agreeing a client workshop agenda with four colleaguesA 41-message reply-all chain. Two people are on leave. "Final" is attached twice, and the version you agree isn't the one attached.One thread in the project channel, six posts, the agreed agenda attached once. The client confirmation goes by email.
Checking whether you can claim a client lunchYou email a colleague and get last year's version, which is out of date.You open the Hub: one policy, approved, current, and searchable.
The team hearing you signed a new clientA private chat with your manager. Two people hear about it.A Ninety.io Headline, so the whole firm hears it at the all-team meeting.
Asking a client a quick question about an invoiceTried in a Teams chat — which can't reach someone outside the firm.Email, because the client is external and needs the record.

Notice that neither column is more work. It's the same work, done somewhere it can be found.

The five places work lives

ChannelUse it forDon't use it for
Outlook emailExternal parties (clients, vendors, partners); anything that needs a formal record or paper trail; formal decisions; firm-wide announcements that need acknowledgmentInternal project coordination, quick internal questions
Teams channel postInternal group work, project discussion, day-to-day decisions, sharing files and linksClient communication, firm-wide announcements
Teams private chatFast, informal questions to one or two peopleProject collaboration and decisions
Ninety.io HeadlineAnything the whole team should see or align on at the next all-team meeting: wins, issues, firm-level updatesUrgent same-day items, one-on-one conversations
SharePoint (the OneAccord Hub)Official reference material you read: policies, resources, trainingAnything that needs a response or decision

The one question

When you're not sure where something goes, ask: does this need a record, a response, or a meeting?

  • A record — or it goes outside the firm: email.
  • A quick internal response: Teams. Private chat for one or two people, a channel post for the team.
  • The team's attention at the next meeting: a Ninety.io Headline.
  • Just reference material: the Hub on SharePoint.

Three names you'll meet in this course:

  • Ninety.io is where OneAccord's all-team meeting runs. A Headline is a short written item you post so it's on the agenda when the whole firm next meets.
  • The Hub is the OneAccord SharePoint site (oneaccord.sharepoint.com/sites/WelcomeOneAccord): the read-only home for approved policies, standards and training. You read and search there; if something should be added or corrected, contact Jesse or Abby.
  • Channels are the topic rooms inside a Teams team — #Wins, #Lessons, #Resources and #Events sit in the company-wide team. You'll work inside channels from Lesson 3.

The point of all five is not tidiness. It's that a decision made in a channel can be found by the person covering for you, and a policy in the Hub is the current one.

blocks.prompt: You need to send a client your revised proposal. Where does it go?
options: A Teams channel post
Outlook email, because the client is outside OneAccord
A Teams private chat
A Ninety.io Headline
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Two reasons, not one: the client is external, and a proposal needs a record of what was sent and when.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The client is outside OneAccord — Teams doesn't reach them — and a proposal needs a record. That's email.

blocks.prompt: A project team of five is deciding next week's task split. Where should that discussion happen?
options: In a private chat between two of them
In a long reply-all email chain
In a post in the project's Teams channel
In a Ninety.io Headline
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. A channel post is visible to all five and searchable next month; a chat reaches two people and email reaches only whoever is copied.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Five people deciding together is internal group work. That's a channel post — visible to everyone on the project and findable later.

blocks.prompt: You need the current, approved travel policy before you book a flight. Where do you look?
options: Ask in a private chat
Search your old emails
The OneAccord Hub on SharePoint
Your local Documents folder
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. The Hub holds the approved version. An email or a chat gives you someone's recollection, which is how people end up claiming the wrong thing.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The Hub is the single source of truth for approved policies. Asking a colleague gets you their memory of it, not the current rule.

blocks.promptHtml:
It's Tuesday morning and four things land on you before 10 a.m.:

  1. A client emails asking you to confirm Thursday's workshop agenda.
  2. You and two colleagues need to decide who presents which section. One of them is travelling and can't join a call.
  3. You've just signed a new client and want the firm to know.
  4. You need the current expense policy before booking travel.

Then, late in the afternoon, a colleague emails five of you about that workshop agenda and two people reply-all.

For each of the four items plus the afternoon thread: say where it goes, why, and what you'd actually do — including what you do with the client's confirmation and what you do with the internal thread so nothing is lost.
rubric: Sends the client's agenda confirmation by Outlook email, because the client is external and a confirmation needs a record
Moves the three-person presentation decision to a post in the project's Teams channel, because a travelling colleague needs to see it and the decision should stay findable — not a chat
Shares the new client as a Ninety.io Headline, so the whole firm sees it at the all-team meeting, rather than an email to everyone
Finds the expense policy in the SharePoint Hub as the approved source, rather than asking a colleague or searching old email

Stops the five-person reply-all thread by copying its content into a channel post, keeps the client-facing confirmation in email, and explains why — history that survives a handover instead of disappearing into inboxes
blocks.coachContext: The five places are email (external parties, formal records, firm-wide announcements needing acknowledgment), Teams channel posts (internal group work and day-to-day decisions), Teams private chat (quick informal questions between one or two people), Ninety.io Headlines (wins, issues and firm-level updates for the all-team meeting) and the SharePoint Hub (read-only approved reference material). The test is: record, response or meeting. The purpose is searchable history that survives leave and role changes. An internal reply-all with more than two people is stopped and restarted as a channel post; a client thread stays in email.

blocks.prompt: A client thread has three OneAccord colleagues on it. One replies-all with an internal question — 'who's covering the data pull?' — that the client doesn't need to see. What's the right move?
options: Reply-all anyway, so the client sees everything that's happening
Keep the client thread in email and take the internal question to the project's Teams channel
Move the whole thread to Teams, client included
Answer it in a private chat and leave no record
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The client thread stays in email, because that's where the client is. The internal question goes where the team can see and find it — a chat would answer it once and lose it.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Split it by audience: the client thread stays in email, and the internal logistics question goes to the project channel, where the team can see the answer.

blocks.prompt: You're on leave for two weeks and a colleague covers your project. Which arrangement actually makes that possible?
options: Everything is in your inbox, plus an out-of-office reply
The discussion and decisions sit in the project channel, the working files are in the team's files, and a short handover note is posted in the channel
You forward your 40 most recent emails before you go
You ask colleagues to call if anything urgent comes up
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. That's the whole point of the Standard: the project's history isn't stored in one person's mailbox. An out-of-office tells people you're away; it doesn't tell them what you decided.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Forwarding email or taking calls still leaves the reasoning in your head and your inbox. The work has to live in the channel and team files for someone else to pick it up.

blocks.label: In the tools
blocks.instructions:
Two short things, in the tools themselves.

1. Find the Hub. Open oneaccord.sharepoint.com/sites/WelcomeOneAccord and find one policy or standard you'll need in your first month (expenses, travel, time off — whichever applies soonest). Note where it sits, so you know where to look next time.

2. Look at the firm's pulse. Open Ninety.io, find the Headlines from the last all-team meeting, and read two of them. That's the channel your own wins and issues will appear in.

If either one isn't open to you yet, note it and raise it with Jesse or Abby rather than working around it.
blocks.confirmText: I've found the Hub and read the last Headlines — continue

blocks.label: Core Takeaway
blocks.title: Lesson 1: The OneAccord Digital Standard
blocks.promptHtml: Put the map in your own words so you'll use it. Your answers are saved in this browser only — they aren't sent to your manager or kept as a grade.

fields.label: In one or two sentences: what does the Standard actually protect — and for whom?
Which single habit will you start this week (for example: stop one internal reply-all and move it to a channel), and when will you do it?
If nothing changed — yours or the firm's — what would it cost? Think about time hunting, a colleague covering for you, or a client seeing an old version.

criteria: The takeaway is in the learner's own words and names a concrete benefit (finding decisions, surviving a handover, a current policy) rather than repeating the five channel names
The commitment is one specific action with a time, not a general intention to 'use the standard'
The cost of not changing is concrete — minutes lost hunting, a decision that can't be reconstructed, or a client receiving the wrong version

blocks.html:
Keep these to hand

The Hub is where the approved version of anything you look up lives. Ninety.io access is set up for you as a new team member — if it isn't open yet, ask Jesse or Abby rather than working around it.

links.label: The OneAccord Hub — approved policies, standards and training

coachPersona: You are an experienced OneAccord colleague coaching a new team member on how the firm organises its work across Outlook, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint (the OneAccord Hub) and Ninety.io. You are not selling software: you are teaching a shared way of working so that decisions can be found, history survives a handover, and clients get a consistent experience. Coach in plain, warm, specific language, and judge judgment and reasoning, not vocabulary. OneAccord's values are truth, compassion and service.
